file.description: The agents file: a YAML list of `{id, name, transport?, cardUrl?, tokenEnv?, agent?, gate?}`, relative to this file's directory. Required unless `registry.url` is set. Replaces `AGENTS_FILE`.

localConcurrency.description: Runs of local agents stepped at once, at least 1 (default 4). A build without the Cargo feature `agent-local` refuses the key. Replaces `AGENT_LOCAL_CONCURRENCY`.

registry.description: The platform's agent registry (`agent-registry/v1`, ADR 0022). A build without the Cargo feature `registry-platform` refuses it.

ArtifactStoreKind.description: Which store keeps the files, one of the implementations of the `ArtifactStore` port. A build that does not have the Cargo feature of the one named refuses it (exit 78), never ignores it.

Artifacts.description: The artifact store (ADR 0032): the files an agent hands over, kept by the hash of their content. The event log keeps only the reference.

fetchHosts.description: The hosts a `url` part of an agent's artifact may be fetched from (`files.example.com`, `10.0.0.5:8080`: a host name or address, with or without a port, no scheme, path, wildcard or credentials). Default none: a `url` part stays a link. A host here is **trusted**: the orchestrator reads a file from it on an agent's say-so, over `http` or `https`, with no redirect followed, no credential sent, within `maxFileBytes`.

fs.description: The directory store. Required with `store: fs`.

maxFileBytes.description: The largest file kept, in bytes: 1 to 268435456 (256 MiB), default 10485760 (10 MiB). A larger file is not kept: the agent's artifact is shown without it, with an error.

maxPerJobBytes.description: The most bytes of files one job keeps (a job is one run of an agent): 1 to 4294967296 (4 GiB), default 104857600 (100 MiB). A job also keeps at most 50 files. A file that would go over either is not kept, like one over `maxFileBytes`.

s3.description: The S3 store. Required with `store: s3`.

store.description: Which store: `fs` (a directory, for development and one node) or `s3` (a bucket). The section of the store chosen is required, and the other one is an error.

root.description: The directory the files are kept in; relative to this file's directory. It is made (mode 0700) when it is not there. The worker that keeps a file and the control plane that serves it must see the same directory: one machine, or a shared volume.

ArtifactsS3.description: The S3 store. The bucket is addressed in the path of the endpoint when there is one, and as a host name of AWS otherwise. The credentials are static: this build does not read `AWS_*` variables or an instance profile.

accessKeyId.description: The access key id, a secret.

bucket.description: The bucket, which must exist: 3 to 63 characters, lower case letters, digits, `-` and `.`, starting and ending with a letter or a digit.

endpoint.description: The server's URL, `http` or `https`, for a server other than AWS (`https://minio.example.com`). Absent: AWS S3 in `region`. An `http` endpoint sends the files in the clear.

prefix.description: A prefix every key is put under (`orchestrator/prod`: `a-z`, `A-Z`, `0-9`, `.`, `_`, `-` and `/`, no `..`, at most 128 characters), so one bucket serves several deployments.

region.description: The region (default `us-east-1`, which S3-compatible servers that have none expect).

secretAccessKey.description: The secret access key, a secret.

timeoutSecs.description: Seconds one request may take, 1 to 3600 (default 60).

Auth.description: Authentication and what a person may do (ADR 0033).

defaultRole.description: The role of a person none of whose roles is one of `roles`: a valid token whose roles claim holds none that is defined here, or no roles claim at all, and every request of the proxy header, which carries none. It must be one of `roles`. Written `null`, nobody gets a role by default: such a person is refused (403) by everything but `GET /api/me`. Absent, it is `user` when `roles` is absent too (so that a deployment that configures nothing is as it was), and `null` when `roles` is given (a deployment that defines its roles names the default, or has none).

devUser.description: The e-mail served for requests without `X-Auth-Request-Email`. Development only: the orchestrator logs a warning, and only `auth.mode: proxy_header` takes it. Replaces `AUTH_DEV_USER`.

jwt.description: The token issuer and what is read from its tokens. Required by the modes that read tokens, refused by `proxy_header`.

mode.description: How a request says who it is from (default `proxy_header`, which changes nothing): `proxy_header` trusts the identity header oauth2-proxy sets (and `devUser`), `jwt` is an OAuth2 resource server that validates the bearer token against the issuer's keys (it needs `jwt`), `jwt_or_proxy_header` takes the token when there is one and the header when there is not (the migration, for one release). A mode whose Cargo feature (`auth-jwt`, `auth-header`) is not in the build is refused.

roles.description: What each role grants, by the name the identity provider gives the role (a group, a realm role: `auth.jwt.rolesClaim`), compared exactly. A role that is not defined here grants nothing. Absent: `user` (everything but `admin`, over one's own threads) and `admin` (also `admin`, and reading every thread, but changing only one's own). Given, it replaces both.

AuthMode.description: How a request says who it is from.

AuthPermission.description: A permission of a role. The names are the platform's (`another-agentic-platform` `docs/architecture/08-security.md`, section 52).

agents.description: The agents `agent.read` and `agent.invoke` are about: agent ids, or `"*"` for every agent (default `["*"]`). An id that no agent has matches nothing. Only with a role that holds one of those two.

permissions.description: The permissions the role holds. Empty: the role is known and grants nothing.

scope.description: How far `thread.read`, `artifact.read` and `thread.write` reach: `own` (the person's own threads), `any` (everyone's), or `{ read, write }` for one scope each (default `own`). Only with a role that holds one of those three.

AuthScope.description: How far a permission over threads reaches.

anyOf.description: `own` or `any`, for reading and for writing alike.
`{ read: any, write: own }`: an administrator who reads everything and changes only their own. Each member defaults to `own`.

AuthScopes.description: The `scope` of a role: one scope for everything, or one for reading and one for writing.

maxConnections.description: The pool size, at least 2: the wakeup listener holds one (default 10). Replaces `DATABASE_MAX_CONNECTIONS`.

url.description: The connection string, a secret. Replaces `DATABASE_URL`.

DescriptionTask.description: The description task: when a job ends or pauses for the person, the model is asked for a sentence or two on what the thread is about now.

endpoint.description: The name of an endpoint in `models.endpoints`.

language.description: The language of the description: the person's (`conversation`, the default) or a fixed one.

maxChars.description: Where a description is cut, at a word: 40 to 500 characters (default 300).

model.description: The model's name at the endpoint.

recompute.description: When a new description is asked for.

system.description: The guidance that says what to write and in what style, in place of the core's own; read once at startup. The core always adds the form of the answer, the data clause, the fence around the conversation and the language line, last, whatever this says.

concurrency.description: Outbox rows processed at once (default 32). Replaces `DISPATCHER_CONCURRENCY`.

outboxLeaseSecs.description: Seconds a crashed replica's claim blocks others, at least 3 (default 30). Also how long a local agent's run stays leased. Replaces `OUTBOX_LEASE_SECS`.

apiKey.description: The bearer token the endpoint wants, when it wants one. Replaces `ORCH_MODEL_API_KEY`.

baseUrl.description: The base URL, up to and not including `/chat/completions`, `http` or `https`. Replaces `ORCH_MODEL_BASE_URL`.

timeoutSecs.description: Seconds one question may take, at least 1 (default 20). Replaces `ORCH_MODEL_TIMEOUT_SECS`.

Environment.description: Where this process runs. `production` makes the configuration refuse what is only for a single user on a local machine.

Gate.description: The deployment's layer of the verification gate. The members have the names of an agent entry's `gate` in the agents file.

ci.description: The CI checks of the deployment's gate.

maxAttempts.description: Attempts a job's agent gets under a gate, the first included, at least 1 and at most `maxAttemptsCap` (default 3, lowered to the cap when the cap is lower). Replaces `ORCH_MAX_ATTEMPTS`.

maxAttemptsCap.description: The most a target or a thread may raise the attempts to, 1 to 100 (default 10). Replaces `ORCH_MAX_ATTEMPTS_CAP`.

require.description: The sources every job's work must pass before it is done (default none: an agent that completes is done). Replaces `ORCH_GATE`.

verifier.description: The agent that verifies the pushed work: the id of another configured agent. Needed when the gate requires `verifier`. Replaces `ORCH_VERIFIER`.

verifierTimeoutSecs.description: Seconds the verifier has to answer before the thread waits for the user, at least 1 (default 1800). Replaces `ORCH_VERIFIER_TIMEOUT_SECS`.

verifierWatchSecs.description: Seconds between a verification's looks at its thread, at least 1 (default 5). Replaces `ORCH_VERIFIER_WATCH_SECS`.

GateCi.description: The CI settings of the deployment's gate.

required.description: The names of the CI checks that must pass: GitHub's check name or workflow name, or the `name` of a generic report. A gate that requires `ci` must name at least one, here or in an agent's `gate.ci.required`. Replaces `ORCH_CI_REQUIRED`.

timeoutSecs.description: Seconds a job waits for the CI reports its gate needs before it is blocked, at least 1 (default 3600). Replaces `ORCH_CI_TIMEOUT_SECS`.

GateSource.description: A source a job's work can be required to pass (ADR 0018). `ci`: CI reports the pushed commit green (needs `gate.ci.required` and a CI webhook surface). `agent-checks`: the agent's own `checks` artifact passes. `verifier`: another agent reviews the pushed commit (needs `gate.verifier`).

leaseSecs.description: Seconds a worker's claim on a row lasts, at least 3 (default 30). Replaces `INBOX_LEASE_SECS`.

maxAttempts.description: Claims of one row before it is given up on, at least 1 (default 10). Replaces `INBOX_MAX_ATTEMPTS`.

parkedTtlSecs.description: Seconds a report that matches no watch waits before it expires, at least 1 (default 86400). Replaces `INBOX_PARKED_TTL_SECS`.

pollSecs.description: Seconds between the worker's polls, at least 1 (default 2). Replaces `INBOX_POLL_SECS`.

Jwt.description: The token issuer, and what is read from its tokens.

audiences.description: The audiences this API accepts: one of them must be among the token's `aud`. With oauth2-proxy passing the ID token this is oauth2-proxy's client id.

issuer.description: The issuer: a token's `iss` must equal it exactly, and unless `jwksUrl` is set its keys are found from `<issuer>/.well-known/openid-configuration`. An `http(s)` URL with no credentials, query or fragment, for example `https://idp.example/realms/main`.

jwksUrl.description: Where the issuer's keys (a JWKS) are, when not in its discovery document.

rolesClaim.description: The path of the claim that holds the person's roles, with dots for the objects on the way: `realm_access.roles` (Keycloak), `groups`. None: no roles. A claim whose own name has dots (`https://example.com/roles`) is found by that name first.

userClaim.description: The claim whose value is the user, and so the owner of what the person creates (default `email`, which keeps the threads that exist). Trimmed and lower-cased.

Language.description: The language a task writes in: `conversation` is the language the person writes in, found in their messages and checked on the answer; any other is fixed, named in the request and checked against its own script. The set is the core's, closed.

Log.description: Logging. The filter is `RUST_LOG`, read before anything else (default `info,rmcp=warn`).

format.description: The format of a log line (default `json`). Replaces `LOG_FORMAT`.

LogFormat.description: The format of a log line: `json`, one object per line, what a log collector wants; or `text`, human-readable lines for local development.

allowedHosts.description: The `Host` values the server accepts, each `host` or `host:port`. Required when `mcp` is mounted by a role that serves routes. Replaces `MCP_ALLOWED_HOSTS`.

allowedOrigins.description: Browser origins let through, each `http(s)://host[:port]` (default none). Replaces `MCP_ALLOWED_ORIGINS`.

tokensFile.description: The tokens file: a YAML list of `{user, tokenEnv}`, relative to this file's directory. Required when `mcp` is mounted by a role that serves routes. Replaces `MCP_TOKENS_FILE`.

waitMaxConcurrent.description: The most `wait_for_job` calls this process holds open, at least 1 (default 256). Replaces `MCP_WAIT_MAX_CONCURRENT`.

waitMaxPerUser.description: The most one user may hold open, at least 1 (default 16). Replaces `MCP_WAIT_MAX_PER_USER`.

endpoints.description: Endpoints by name (a slug: `a-z`, `0-9` and `-`, up to 32 characters). The legacy `ORCH_MODEL_*` variables are the endpoint named `default`.

Prompt.description: A prompt, given inline or by file: `{ inline: TEXT }` or `{ file: PATH }` (a relative path is relative to the directory of the configuration file). UTF-8, 1 to 4096 bytes once the space around it is cut. A file is read once, at startup.

oneOf.description: The path of a file that holds the text.

Recompute.description: When a new description is asked for.

minNewMessages.description: How many messages (of the person, and the agent's final words) the conversation has to have grown by since the last description before a new one is asked for, at least 1 (default 4). Fewer is no model call.

Registry.description: The platform's agent registry, read live beside the agents file.

agentToken.description: The bearer token sent to every agent the registry lists. Replaces `AGENT_REGISTRY_AGENT_TOKEN`.

maxAgeSecs.description: The most seconds a copy of the document is kept, 1 to 3600 (default 60). Replaces `AGENT_REGISTRY_MAX_AGE_SECS`.

timeoutSecs.description: Seconds one read may take, 1 to 60 (default 3). Replaces `AGENT_REGISTRY_TIMEOUT_SECS`.

token.description: The bearer token sent to the registry, when it wants one. Replaces `AGENT_REGISTRY_TOKEN`.

url.description: The full URL of the document, `http` or `https`, with a host and no user name or password. Replaces `AGENT_REGISTRY_URL`.

Role.description: What this process runs. A closed enum owned by the host library (`adam-host`); the names are the same for every host. `all`: the control plane and the workers, in one process. `control-plane`: the HTTP server, the resource API and the surfaces, no dispatcher. `worker`: the dispatcher, and a router with only `/healthz` and `/readyz`.

SecretRef.description: A reference to a secret: where its value is read from at startup, never the value. `{ env: NAME }` reads the environment variable `NAME` (it must be set and not empty); `{ file: PATH }` reads the file at `PATH` (a relative path is relative to the directory of the configuration file; one trailing newline is cut; at most 64 KiB). A plain string where a secret goes is an error.

oneOf.description: The name of an environment variable that holds the secret.
The path of a file that holds the secret.

Server.description: The process: where it listens, what it runs, what it mounts.

environment.description: `development` (default) or `production`. A `production` process refuses `auth.mode: proxy_header` (and so `auth.devUser`): the identity header is only as good as the proxy that strips it (ADR 0033).

instanceId.description: Names this replica in outbox leases (default `$HOSTNAME-<uuid>`). `ORCH_INSTANCE_ID` and `--instance-id` stay as a process override.

listen.description: The socket address to listen on (default `0.0.0.0:8080`). Replaces `LISTEN_ADDR`.

publicUrl.description: The public origin of the chat, for example `https://chat.example.com`: the MCP surface gives `start_job` a `web_url` from it. Replaces `ORCH_PUBLIC_URL`.

role.description: What this process runs (default `all`). `ORCH_ROLE` and `--role` stay as a process override: a control plane and its workers share one file.

shutdownGraceSecs.description: Seconds a graceful shutdown may take (default 15). Replaces `SHUTDOWN_GRACE_SECS`.

surfaces.description: The surfaces to mount, as far as the build has them (default `[agui]`). Replaces `ORCH_SURFACES`.

SplitScope.description: A scope for reading (`thread.read`, `artifact.read`) and one for writing (`thread.write`).

recordToolIo.description: Whether a step's input and output (what a tool was called with and what it returned) are recorded in the log, redacted and capped (ADR 0030; default `true`). Replaces `ORCH_STEPS_RECORD_IO`.

Surface.description: An interaction surface: a set of HTTP routes the orchestrator can mount. `agui`: the AG-UI routes the web speaks (ADR 0012). `mcp`: the MCP server at `/mcp` (ADR 0019; needs `mcp.tokensFile` and `mcp.allowedHosts`). `thread-tools`: the per-thread MCP endpoint (`thread-tools/v1`; needs `threadTools.url` and `secret`). `webhook-generic`: `POST /webhooks/ci`, the generic signed CI report (needs `webhooks.generic`). `webhook-github`: `POST /webhooks/github`, GitHub's own deliveries (needs `webhooks.github`).

Tasks.description: The utility tasks: what the orchestrator asks a model for on its own account, each with the endpoint, model, prompt and language rule it runs with (ADR 0035). A task that is absent is off.

description.description: The thread description. Absent: threads have none.

title.description: The thread title. Absent: titles are off.

allowedHosts.description: The `Host` values the endpoint accepts, each `host` or `host:port` (default: the host of `url`). Replaces `THREAD_TOOLS_ALLOWED_HOSTS`.

previousSecret.description: The previous key, for verifying only (a rotation): a secret of at least 32 bytes, not the current one. Replaces `THREAD_TOOLS_SECRET_PREVIOUS`.

secret.description: The HMAC key of the tokens, a secret of at least 32 bytes. Replaces `THREAD_TOOLS_SECRET`.

tokenTtlSecs.description: Seconds a token lives, 60 to 86400 (default 7200). Replaces `THREAD_TOOLS_TOKEN_TTL_SECS`.

url.description: The base URL under which agents reach this orchestrator, `http` or `https`. Both or neither of `url` and `secret`. Replaces `THREAD_TOOLS_URL`.

TitleTask.description: The title task: after the agent's first reply, the model is asked for a 3 to 6 word title.

endpoint.description: The name of an endpoint in `models.endpoints`.

language.description: The language of the title: the person's (`conversation`, the default) or a fixed one.

model.description: The model's name at the endpoint. Replaces `ORCH_TITLE_MODEL`.

system.description: The guidance that says what to write and in what style, in place of the core's own; read once at startup. The core always adds the form of the answer, the data clause, the fence around the conversation and the language line, last, whatever this says.

Ui.description: What the web is told about how to show things: the one part of the file it can read, served as `GET /api/config` (ADR 0034). **It has no secret and never will**: a test asserts that its schema holds no secret reference.

showDescriptions.description: Whether the web shows a thread's description (default true). The API returns it either way.

maxSkewSecs.description: Seconds the `X-Vymalo-Timestamp` may differ from the clock, either way, at least 1 (default 300). Replaces `WEBHOOK_GENERIC_MAX_SKEW_SECS`.

secrets.description: One or two shared secrets, each at least 32 bytes: a report is accepted when its signature matches either, so a secret can be rotated. Replaces `WEBHOOK_GENERIC_SECRETS` (one variable holding one or two comma-separated secrets).

maxAgeSecs.description: Seconds old the signed completion time of an event may be, at least 1 (default 86400). Replaces `WEBHOOK_GITHUB_MAX_AGE_SECS`.

secrets.description: One or two secrets of the GitHub webhook, each at least 32 bytes. Replaces `WEBHOOK_GITHUB_SECRETS` (one variable holding one or two comma-separated secrets).

generic.description: `POST /webhooks/ci`. Required when the surface `webhook-generic` is mounted by a role that serves routes.

github.description: `POST /webhooks/github`. Required when the surface `webhook-github` is mounted by a role that serves routes.

agents.description: The agents: a file, in-process agents, the platform's registry.

artifacts.description: The artifact store: where the files agents hand over are kept (ADR 0032). Absent: no store, and a file an agent hands over is refused with "no artifact store configured".

database.description: The Postgres database, the one place the system keeps state.

dispatcher.description: The dispatcher: the outbox rows worked at once, and the lease on them.

gate.description: The deployment's layer of the verification gate (ADR 0018).

inbox.description: The inbox worker: timers and stored reports.

models.description: The OpenAI-compatible endpoints the orchestrator asks itself (ADR 0005, ADR 0035).

server.description: The process: the address it listens on, its role, the interaction surfaces it mounts.

tasks.description: The utility tasks that use a model: a task that is absent is off (ADR 0035).

threadTools.description: The thread tools: the endpoint agents call back, and the key of its tokens.

version.description: The version of this file's format. This build reads `1`.
